rav-tovi-bar-mattana.name: Rav Tovi bar Mattana
rav-tovi-bar-mattana.bio: Babylonian Amora who transmits Rabbi Yoshiya’s source for the law of set-aside (Temurah 29a).
rav-tovi-bar-mattana.prompt: A sage in his 50s with a greying beard and a plain dark wool mantle, reciting a teaching he received with one hand resting on an open scroll; background of a Babylonian study hall with mud-brick walls and an oil lamp.

rabbi-yoshiya-amora.name: Rabbi Yoshiya
rabbi-yoshiya-amora.bio: Amora, not the Tanna of the same name, whose derivation of the law of set-aside from “you shall safeguard” Rav Tovi bar Mattana transmits (Temurah 29a).
rabbi-yoshiya-amora.prompt: A sage in his 60s with a long white beard and a cream wool mantle, pointing to a line of an open scroll as he expounds a verse; background of a study hall with pale stone walls and a lamp in a niche.

rava-bar-rav-adda.name: Rava bar Rav Adda
rava-bar-rav-adda.bio: Babylonian Amora who transmits Rav Yitzḥak’s ruling on how long an animal set aside for idol worship stays prohibited (Temurah 29a).
rava-bar-rav-adda.prompt: A sage in his 40s with a short dark beard and a russet wool mantle, repeating a ruling with a finger raised as he names its source; background of a Babylonian study hall with mud-brick walls and seated students.

rav-yitzchak.name: Rav Yitzḥak
rav-yitzchak.bio: Amora cited in the Talmud by this name alone.
rav-yitzchak.prompt: A sage in his 50s with a greying beard and a plain brown wool mantle, answering a colleague with a calm open hand; background of a study hall with stone walls and an oil lamp.

baha.name: Baha
baha.era: Amora · Babylonia and the Land of Israel
baha.bio: Amora who went up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel and transmits a ruling of Rabbi Yoḥanan on set-aside (Temurah 29a).
baha.prompt: A sage in his 40s with a dark beard and a travel-worn wool mantle over a scholar’s robe, explaining a teaching with both hands open; background of a study hall in the Land of Israel with pale stone walls and a window onto hills.

rabbi-chananya-terita.name: Rabbi Ḥananya Terita
rabbi-chananya-terita.bio: Amora who taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan: on Temurah 29a he teaches and explains a ruling on set-aside, and on 31a, where the text calls him Rabbi Ḥanina Terita, he explains Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus’s ruling on an animal that suckled from a tereifa.
rabbi-chananya-terita.prompt: A sage in his 40s with a trimmed dark beard and a plain grey wool mantle, reciting a teaching from memory before his teacher with one hand keeping its rhythm; background of a study hall in Tiberias with stone arches.

rav-chanan-bar-rav-chisda.name: Rav Ḥanan bar Rav Ḥisda
rav-chanan-bar-rav-chisda.bio: Babylonian Amora, son of Rav Ḥisda.
rav-chanan-bar-rav-chisda.prompt: A sage in his 40s with a dark beard and a deep blue wool mantle, resolving a contradiction with two fingers raised to set two cases apart; background of a Babylonian study hall with mud-brick walls and a single oil lamp.
